name: Jack Straw
description: Named by several contemporary chroniclers as a rebel leader active in the early Essex and Kentish phases of the revolt, and by some accounts captured and executed in London afterward. Modern historians flag his identity as a genuine, unresolved open question: it is unclear whether 'Jack Straw' names a real, distinct individual or is a chronicler's alias for Wat Tyler or for John Wrawe. This book treats the identity question as an honest gap in the record rather than resolving it either way.
narrative_function: A name attached to real events whose referent cannot be confirmed -- an explicit example of the record's limits.
